story: On a sunny Thursday evening at 7:17, Gary strides off toward Town Hall with a determined look, while Donna and Hal chat happily with Rosa on Magnolia Loop. Donna is cheerfully promising her famous deviled eggs for Friday dinner and planning to trim her flamingo collection down to three, with Hal keeping the count. Rosa is reminding everyone that dinner is at her place at six, with Gary bringing cornbread and a chair saved for each of them. Hal promises he'll be on time and leave his flamingo tally at the door.

gary.thought_process: I just looked over the parade sign-up sheet and entry rules, and Rosa's headed off, so nobody's around to talk to. My cart lights and sound system have to be official before the parade, and L-01 says exterior modifications visible from the street need Architectural Review approval. Hal already offered to check my paperwork line by line, and I wrote the ten o'clock cutoff in for L-03 so the sound system stays legal. Town Hall is right off the square, so the best use of this hour is to head over and get the filing going instead of standing around the bandstand. That's the useful thing to do.

parameters.content: Heading to Town Hall to file my golf cart modification paperwork for Architectural Review before the parade.

donna.thought_process: Hal is out here counting my flamingos for the committee file, and Rosa just walked up. I already promised Hal I'd trim the flock to three before Friday, so I shouldn't repeat myself or argue. Better to bring Rosa in warmly, confirm Friday dinner, and keep Hal in a good mood so he shows up to cheer at Gary's first practice tomorrow at ten. Keeping the social scene friendly is what I do best.

parameters.content: Rosa, honey, perfect timing! Hal's tallying my flamingos, so I'm pulling them down to three before Friday dinner, and I'm bringing my famous deviled eggs. You'll come cheer at Gary's first practice tomorrow at ten too, won't you?

hal.thought_process: Donna already promised to trim the flock to three before Friday, and I told her the clipboard stays in the drawer. A man who keeps his word doesn't nag. Rosa just walked up, so I'll be civil and fold in Friday dinner at her place, which I'm looking forward to. Bit of dry humor, no repeating the flamingo lecture.

parameters.content: Evening, Rosa. Friday dinner still on? I'll be there on time, and I'll leave the flamingo count at the door.

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Hal are both right here on Magnolia Loop, and Friday's dinner is tomorrow at six. Gary's cornbread is confirmed, and my memories say Hal and Donna both said yes, but a quick in-person confirmation never hurts and it's the kind of warm nudge that builds community. I shouldn't repeat my invite to Gary. Donna has the courts at ten and I want to make sure she knows dinner is after, so I'll address her first and keep it short, then include Hal as we chat. Plain and friendly, no pressure.

parameters.content: Evening, Donna! Hal, you too. Just a reminder, Friday at six at my place. Gary's bringing cornbread, and I've got a chair saved for each of you. Anything you need me to know about, allergies or such?

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
